UnitStatement: An agent is defined operationally as an LLM plus instructions plus access to files plus use of tools.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: The agent definition is operational, not metaphysical; it describes a kind of runtime system, not a responsible person or bearer of professional duty.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: A good agent is expressed as good_agent = agent_1(agent_2), where Agent 1 orchestrates the instructions for Agent 2.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Good agents do one type of thing really well, and only that one type of thing.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Orchestrating specialized agents between decision points yields speed and trustworthy output for professional engineering work.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: A great agent is expressed as great_agent = agent_0(agent_1(agent_2)), where Agent 0 brings the human and Agent 1 into alignment.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Only three layers of nested agents are needed; more complex architectures can exist but have tradeoffs.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Agent 0, the Architect, writes and maintains the instructions after the human determines alignment.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Agent 1, the Manager, orchestrates which instructions, files, and tools go to which specialist.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Agent 2, the Specialist, takes actions according to instructions.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: In Chirality, an AI agent is a bounded artificial actor that can read files, use tools, generate claims, and modify project state within its write scope.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: In regulated practice, the agent is treated as one of the 'others' whose work a human professional supervises and reviews before relying on it.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: What kind of system an agent is: an agent in the technical sense (LLM + instructions + files + tools).
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: How an agent's work is treated: as delegated work under human supervision, review, and accountability.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: The human remains the accountable party; the agent contributes content and action inside a governed workflow, and the human decides what to rely on.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Trust through specialization: narrowing the scope of Agent 2 reduces the probability of hallucination because it only needs to know how to execute the specific function Agent 1 handed it.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Human authority at every gate: agents propose and humans decide; no agent can approve deliverables, resolve conflicts, or issue work for reliance, and the human stays in responsible charge.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Speed: smaller contexts and specialized instructions process faster and cheaper than massive, general-purpose prompts.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Debuggability: bad output is fixed at Agent 2's tools.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Debuggability: a wrong task attempted is fixed at Agent 1's instructions.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Debuggability: a misunderstood goal is fixed at Agent 0's alignment.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: A team of agents is not just a software pattern; in Chirality it is a project-management structure.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: The decomposition, folder hierarchy, stable IDs, lifecycle states, dependencies, gates, reviews, and change controls are the same organizational devices a human team uses, made directly inspectable in the filesystem.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Many-agent orchestration matters not only for parallelism but for making delegated work legible enough for a human to supervise, review, and accept responsibility for the result.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: In the fan-out/fan-in pattern, the human interfaces with a single Agent 1 instance through chat, and Agent 1 assigns tasks to nested Agent 2 instances running in parallel.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Fan-Out: Agent 1 receives direction from the human and assigns tasks to Agent 2 instances.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Process: Agent 2 instances execute simultaneously.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Fan-In: Agent 1 collects results and returns the final output to the human.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Isolation of failure: if one Agent 2 instance crashes, the others continue unaffected.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Context hygiene: each Agent 2 instance spawns with zero state, preventing context drift from previous tasks.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: In the invoice-processing example, the human directs Agent 1 to process the invoices in a folder.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Agent 1 assigns the task to Agent 2 instances that each extract Date, Amount, and Vendor from a single PDF, then collects and merges the results into a CSV.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: All of the example work is done by Agent 2 types, orchestrated by Agent 1.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.

UnitStatement: Summary: good agents do one thing well, great agents are composed of good agents, and the human decides what to rely on.
CategoryAssignmentRationale: Assigned by G3BR-002: product doc SRC-DOCS-WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT -> CAT-012.
